BIOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: BIOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Response and Coordination 2.2 Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Response and Coordination 2.2 Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Response and Coordination 2.2 Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Response and Coordination 2.2 Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Response and Coordination 2.2 Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of.

2. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Removing all vegetation

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 100 °C

4. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Only carbon dioxide

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AND BIODIVERSITY S? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AND BIODIVERSITY S.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AND BIODIVERSITY S.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AND BIODIVERSITY S.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AND BIODIVERSITY S.

6. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Ice melting to water

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Support and Movement in Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Support and Movement in Animals.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Support and Movement in Animals.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Support and Movement in Animals.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Support and Movement in Animals.

8. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Response and Coordination 3.2 Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: C? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Response and Coordination 3.2 Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: C.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Response and Coordination 3.2 Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: C.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Response and Coordination 3.2 Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: C.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Response and Coordination 3.2 Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: C.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Response and Coor? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Response and Coor.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Response and Coor.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Response and Coor.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Response and Coor.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Response and Coordination in Plants? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Response and Coordination in Plants.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Response and Coordination in Plants.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Response and Coordination in Plants.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Response and Coordination in Plants.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Support in Plants? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Support in Plants.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Support in Plants.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Support in Plants.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Support in Plants.

13. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Response and Coordination in Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Response and Coordination in Animals.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Response and Coordination in Animals.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Response and Coordination in Animals.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Response and Coordination in Animals.

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Genetics? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Genetics.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Genetics.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Genetics.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Genetics.

16. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. joule (J)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

17. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

18. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

19. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

20. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Evolution? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Evolution.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Evolution.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Evolution.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Evolution.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS

27. In three clear sentences, explain Support and Movement in Animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

28. In three clear sentences, explain Genetics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
